items.title: Walmart Full Year Forecast; Bath & Body Works Beats Estimates; Stock Movers
items.summary: On this episode of Stock Movers: - Walmart (WMT) shares are reacting to news that the company raised its full-year forecasts for sales and earnings as its focus on prices and e-commerce expansion continue to win over shoppers. Walmart's earnings report suggests that US consumers are still spending ahead of the holiday shopping season. - Bath & Body Works (BBWI) shares are moving after it reported adjusted earnings per share for the third quarter that beat the average analyst estimate. - Palo Alto Networks (PAWN) shares are gaining after the cybersecurity firm delivered better-than-expected first-quarter results and raised its full-year outlook. It also agreed to buy the AI model platform Applied Compute in an $4.5 billion deal that's expected to move the firm into the neocloud business and enable development of cyber-specific AI models.

items.title: Walmart Benefits from E-Commerce
items.summary: Walmart raised its full-year forecasts for sales and earnings, as the retailer's focus on prices and a steady expansion of e-commerce continue to win over shoppers across income groups. Walmart benefited from a boost in its e-commerce business, which grew 23% in the US in the recent quarter. The company is prioritizing faster delivery times, and says it can now deliver to 60% of US households in less than 30 minutes. Sarah Henry, Managing Director and Portfolio Manager at Logan Capital Management, discusses the e-commerce strategy, and whether large-scale, global companies like Walmart should be valued as tech stocks. She speaks with Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu.
